To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of plasticity with elastic degradation results in the loss of uniqueness of incremental response, and that this loss of uniqueness can be caused by a limit point singularity.

(1) combined plasticity and degradation is a nonassociative material model; (2) the tangent operator has a rank-one update of the plastic tensor and a rank-one update (or two rank-one updates) of the current elastic stiffness tensor; (3) the singularity condition for the combined material model is determined by the interaction of the hardening parameters of plasticity and degradation.

The combination of plastic deformation and elastic degradation may result in a limit point singularity of the incremental response, and that the interaction of these two dissipation processes may activate the limit singularity when both dissipation processes are hardening.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How does the interaction of two dissipation processes influence the constitutive singularity of the combined model?
